input: Install blackout curtains in the master bedroom

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing how many windows are involved changes the quantity of curtains, hardware, and total effort required.
Budget determines which curtain brands, materials, and hardware options are realistic to recommend.
Whether curtain rods and brackets are already installed affects whether this is purely a hanging task or also a hardware-mounting task.
The user's comfort with drilling into walls determines whether professional installation should be part of the plan.
Preferred color, fabric weight, and curtain style (grommet, rod pocket, tab top) affect purchasing decisions and the look of the room.
Understanding whether the priority is maximum light blocking, aesthetics, noise reduction, or all three shapes which products to prioritize.
If a partner or housemate has input on style or placement, the planning and approval steps need to be factored in before purchasing.

gold.taskTitle: Install blackout curtains in the master bedroom
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to buy and/or hang blackout curtains in their master bedroom, covering all steps from selection to final installation.

questions.title: How many windows need curtains in the bedroom?
questions.description: The number of windows directly determines how many curtain panels and how much hardware to buy.

questions.title: What is your budget for this project?
questions.description: A rough spending limit helps narrow down curtain brands, fabric quality, and hardware tier.

questions.title: Do you already have curtain rods and brackets installed?
questions.description: Knowing whether hardware is already in place determines if wall drilling and mounting are part of the task.

questions.title: Are you comfortable drilling into walls yourself?
questions.description: The user's DIY confidence affects whether professional installation needs to be sourced and scheduled.

questions.title: Do you have a preferred color, fabric, or curtain style?
questions.description: Style preferences such as color, opacity level, and hanging style (grommet, rod pocket, etc.) shape the purchasing shortlist.

questions.title: What is the main reason you want blackout curtains?
questions.description: Whether the driver is light blocking, better sleep, heat insulation, or noise reduction determines which product features to prioritize.

questions.title: Does anyone else need to approve the curtain choice?
questions.description: If a partner or housemate has a say, a review and approval step must be built into the plan before any purchase is made.
